title: The Enterprise GenAI Stack, Layer by Layer
subtitle: A Thought-Leadership Series on Building GenAI That Regulated Firms Can Trust
author: Bing Zhang
kicker: The view at end of Q3 2026
made_note: This book grew from a LinkedIn series based on an independent review of the enterprise GenAI stack. The research and drafting were carried out with Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic, under the author's direction. Anthropic's products are treated like every other vendor's, and wherever one is named, an independent alternative is named beside it.
cover_tagline: Twenty-five short chapters on building GenAI that regulated firms can trust
back_title: Own the control plane. Rent the components.
blurb: GenAI in a regulated firm is not a model choice. It is a control system: who may call what, on whose behalf, at what cost, with what evidence, and how to leave a vendor without starting again.

This book grew from a LinkedIn series that took the enterprise GenAI stack apart one layer at a time, from foundation models to evaluation, and paired each layer with the control that makes it safe. Each chapter opens with the post, then goes behind it: the evidence, the trade-offs, what good looks like, the honest objections and the questions to take to your team.
One worked example runs throughout and grows chapter by chapter: an agent that drafts a fund's monthly performance-attribution commentary, with a portfolio manager approving every draft.
back_points: Nine layers and eight controls, each in a short, self-contained chapter
A worked example built step by step, from the brief to sign-off
The signal to measure for every layer, with a starting target
Questions to take to your team, chapter by chapter
Vendor-neutral judgement, backed by sourced footnotes
